cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I sealed the first complaint in a brown envelope like yours. I'll admit it stayed in my drawer. Where's the second?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine went to the solicitor. Sealing it wasn't the same as hiding it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, confidential handling. Mine stopped at the drawer. Is that the whole trail?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The second went, yes. There's a third letter on my desk that I haven't forwarded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've admitted keeping mine. Say why yours stayed on the desk.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies an envelope but explicitly knows it stayed hidden; B2 contrasts sending and hiding, yet the scene does not securely show A misunderstood the sealing process. A3 confidence may be concealment alone.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 sent second letter now causes A3 whole-trail question; B4 held third causes A5 reciprocal motive request.

relationship.evidence: B4 volunteers an unforwarded third item, making reciprocity plausible.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 admission as the last missing explanation without falsely claiming its own reason was supplied.

specificity.evidence: A1 drawer, B2 solicitor and B4 desk locate all three letters clearly.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 direct request replaces the inaccurate claim of an already stated motive.
